title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Jordan Reyes
body:
Purpose and scope

This playbook is a consolidated sales enablement reference for Redwood Inference field reps, solutions engineers, and GTM partners. It covers core positioning and messaging, competitive brief talking points, a recommended pitch deck outline, pricing guidance and examples, two exemplar case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this document as the single source for customer-facing narratives and deal play execution.

1) Executive positioning and elevator pitches

Short elevator (for discovery / cold outreach)
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered applications predictable, economical, and reliable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes.

Value proposition (30	20s)
- For engineering teams who need production-grade LLM inference, Redwood provides a unified runtime, model catalog, and operations tooling that deliver low latency, predictable cost, and flexible deployment (hosted, dedicated, private). Unlike single-mode vendors, Redwood unifies the same API, observability, and rollout controls across environments so you can scale from prototype to regulated production without reengineering.

Key differentiators (messaging pillars)
- Production-first performance: GPU-optimized serving runtime, continuous batching, and KV caching tuned for low p99 latency at scale.
- Unified interface: Same API and rollout semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Cost-aware controls: Batching, caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce unit economics without sacrificing quality.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: Smart routing, model fallbacks, and SLA-backed Dedicated options keep customer apps online.
- Developer experience: SDKs, quickstarts, and per-route observability to iterate quickly.

Target personas and pain points
- ML Engineers / Infra: Need predictable latency, efficient GPU utilization, and model lifecycle controls.
- Product Engineers: Need simple API and predictable cost per feature.
- Platform / SRE: Need multi-tenant controls, RBAC, and auditability for enterprise adoption.

2) Competitive brief: positioning vs common competitor classes

Competitor class: General cloud AI platforms
- How they position: Broad managed services + model hosting; deep integrations with cloud provider services.
- Redwood rebuttal: Cloud providers are broad but not opinionated for LLM inference economics \u2014 Redwood offers a runtime tuned for modern attention patterns, kernel selection, and production batching that consistently outperforms generic endpoints on latency/cost for inference-heavy workloads.

Competitor class: LLM API providers (simplicity-first)
- How they position: Quick dev experience and curated models.
- Redwood rebuttal: We match the developer experience while adding predictable throughput, private deployments, and observability required for production SLAs. For customers who outgrow a convenience API, Redwood avoids the forklift.

Competitor class: Self-hosted inference runtimes / OSS stacks
- How they position: Full control and lower unit cost at scale.
- Redwood rebuttal: Self-hosting can yield savings but at high engineering cost (ops, reliability, and model upgrades). Redwood provides reserved Dedicated and Private options that deliver control with managed operational scaffolding and expert support.

One-slide competitive cheat sheet (talking points)
- When to recommend Redwood: mission-critical features requiring SLOs, customers with multi-region or regulated needs, customers who want controlled unit economics and per-route observability.
- When competitor may be OK: very early experiments, no latency/SLO needs, or teams willing to invest in full infra ownership.

3) Pitch deck recommended outline (12	18 slides)

1. Title / hook: short value prop + customer logo if applicable
2. Problem statement: cost, latency, reliability, model lifecycle pain
3. Redwood solution overview: three deployment modes + single API
4. Architecture at a glance: runtime, smart routing, caching, monitoring
5. Performance benchmarks: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec vs compiled alternatives (call out test harness and conditions)
6. Cost controls: batching, caching, quantization profiles and impact examples
7. Security & compliance: data residency, audit logging, KMS integration, SOC/ISO statements (summary)
8. Case study #1: SaaS search (metrics + outcomes)
9. Case study #2: FinServ virtual assistant (metrics + outcomes)
10. Integrations & SDKs: languages, frameworks, infra options
11. Rollout plan: pilot -> canary -> production -> SLA options
12. Pricing snapshot + procurement steps
13. Support & SLA levels: hosted vs dedicated vs private
14. Next steps / demo request / contact

Sales tips for presenting the deck
- Keep early slides engineering-focused when talking to ML / platform teams; shift to outcomes (ROI, time-to-value) for product leaders and execs.
- Always include a short appendix with benchmark methodology and model versions used.

4) Pricing guidance and example plays

Pricing model summary (talking points)
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token for generation, per-embedding unit). Good for trials and early production.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity with monthly/annual commits for predictable throughput and cost. Includes config controls and SLA.
- Private: enterprise licensing and deployment fee for VPC/on-prem with optional support tiers and compliance add-ons.

Guidance: Packaging and negotiation levers
- Start customers on a 3-month pilot in Hosted with usage caps and telemetry to baseline latency and token consumption.
- For customers with steady high throughput, model a Dedicated commit showing unit economics vs Hosted at target QPS and tokens/day.
- Offer pilot-to-reserved credits: convert a portion of pilot spend to committed discounts on Dedicated.

Sample pricing scenarios (examples for sales conversations)
- Small SaaS app (prototype -> production): Hosted, 200k tokens/day avg, p95 latency target 800ms. Estimated monthly: $X (provide internal calculator link).
- Mid-market product team: Dedicated 2x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, predictable 10M tokens/day, includes autoscale buffer + 9x9 support. Example: commit term 12 months, monthly commit $Y with 20% pilot credit.
- Enterprise regulated customer: Private deployment + platform license + optional managed services for onboarding. Typical procurement includes 6\u201312 week deployment, KMS/HSM review, and security questionnaire completion.

Pricing artifacts to share
- Public pricing snapshot (hosted); Dedicated sizing worksheet; Procurement checklist; SOW template.

5) Case studies (condensed battlecards)

Case study A \u2014 SaaS search provider (mid-market)
- Challenge: search feature cost and tail latency at 5M queries/day.
- Solution: Migrated ranking + generation to Redwood Dedicated with KV prefix caching and quantized model variant.
- Outcome: 35% reduction in per-query inference cost, 40% lower p95 latency, achieved 99.95% uptime SLA.
- Sales play: Offer a 6-week cost/latency pilot with a migration checklist and sample data size estimation.

Case study B \u2014 Financial services virtual assistant (regulated)
- Challenge: Data residency, audit logs, and ability to host inference in customer VPC.
- Solution: Private deployment with customer-managed KMS, audit logging enabled, and per-route RBAC.
- Outcome: Passed internal security review, reduced time-to-market for the assistant by 3 months, delivered 99.9% intent recognition accuracy improvement over legacy rules.
- Sales play: Align security/compliance stakeholders early; provide architecture reference and checklist from eng-private-deployments.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise, prospect-facing answers)

Q: Where is customer data stored and processed?
A: Hosted API processes inference in our multi-region hosted clusters; customers can select region(s) for data residency. For regulated workloads, Dedicated and Private deployments keep inference and logs within customer-owned or dedicated infrastructure.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. Private and Dedicated options support KMS integrations and HSM-backed key material for encryption-at-rest and key lifecycle management.

Q: How do you handle audit logging and access controls?
A: We provide per-request audit logs, role-based access controls (RBAC), and can export logs to customer SIEMs. Private deployments offer full control of logging endpoints.

Q: What compliance attestations do you have?
A: We maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness for enterprise customers. For detailed evidence packages and responsibility matrices, request our compliance binder via Sales Ops.

Q: How is PII or sensitive data protected during inference?
A: We recommend a defense-in-depth approach: minimize sensitive tokens in prompts, use tokenization redaction in client libraries, enable encryption in transit and at rest, and consider Private deployment for strict data residency needs. We also offer prompt-level masking tools in Redwood Console.

Q: What is the incident response and breach notification process?
A: Incident response follows our Security Incident Response playbook with defined SLAs for notification. For Dedicated and Private customers, we provide a contact escalation path and post-incident reports.

7) Deal execution plays and go-to-market steps

Standard pilot -> pilot-to-dedicated motion
1. Discovery: collect telemetry needs, target latency, compliance constraints.
2. Pilot scoping: select model(s), estimate tokens/day, and choose deployment mode (Hosted pilot recommended).
3. Pilot execution: provide onboarding guide, quickstart, and SRE contact. Track p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics.
4. Review & decision: present pilot results; recommend Dedicated sizing if sustained throughput or Private if regulatory constraints.
5. Contracting: offer pilot credit convert + standard SOW and onboarding timeline.

Support bundles and SLA options
- Standard (hosted): 9x5 email + community support, 99.9% platform availability target.
- Premium (dedicated): 24x7 support, 99.95% availability SLA, dedicated support engineers.
- Enterprise (private): dedicated TAM, white-glove onboarding, quarterly QBRs, on-call escalation path.

9) Appendix: negotiation playbook and objection handling

Common objections and rebuttals
- \"We can self-host cheaper\": Outline total cost of ownership, time-to-value metrics, and list operational labor required. Offer a cost comparison workshop.
- \"We only need a simple API\": Recommend Hosted with conservative pilot caps and emphasize easy migration to Dedicated/Private without changing application code.
- \"We need strict data residency\": Walk through Private deployment offering, timeline, and pre-approved reference architecture.

Negotiation levers (commercial)
- Pilot credits, multi-year committed discounts, professional services hours for migration, phased payment schedules, and limited-term SLAs.

Document ownership and next steps

- Document owner: Jordan Reyes (go-to-market). For updates, submit PR to the sales enablement team channel with reviewer sign-off from product and security.

End of playbook.
